Sean McVay's team has spent three weeks digging out of a 2-4 start, and the national experts are convinced the Los Angeles Rams will make it four straight Sunday in Glendale. They also remember what happened the last time these two met. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16 at SoFi Stadium in Week 6.
 That game was played with Puka Nacua. This one won't be, since he and Davante Adams are both on injured reserve. Arizona is starting rookie Carson Beck in his NFL debut, and nobody we found thinks that's a fair fight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement NFL.com sees a low-scoring win
 Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett (95) looks on during the first quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn ImagesGeoff Burke-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
 All five NFL.com editors picked the Rams : Bobby Kownack (21-7), Dan Parr (24-14), Jeremy Bergman (20-10), Brooke Cersosimo (25-17) and Gennaro Filice (19-13). None of them has Los Angeles scoring more than 25.
 Cersosimo called them "big road favorites in the desert" and pointed to Myles Garrett, who had three sacks and a forced fumble in his return against Washington.
 Garrett is questionable with a knee issue, though Sean McVay said Friday he expects him to play . "He's feeling good," McVay said. "It's more of just getting him feeling as good as possible."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement ESPN and SI agree
 ESPN's Pamela Maldonado (23-16), Eric Moody (27-17) and Aaron Schatz (27-20) all took the Rams, and ESPN's FPI gives Los Angeles an 87.4% chance to win. Sports Illustrated's 10-person panel, including Albert Breer and Conor Orr, went 10-for-10 on the Rams .
 Bleacher Report was just as sure. All seven of its NFL writers took the Rams to cover , and Maurice Moton expects them to bracket Trey McBride and wear down Arizona's front to avenge that loss.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Average the five NFL.com scores and the Rams win by 9.6 points. FPI projects 11.5. Set those next to the two-point game Arizona won in October, and the gap shows how much the experts think has changed in four weeks.
 What Arizona did in Week 6
 Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) pressures Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) in the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images
 The Cardinals have the second-worst pass block win rate in the league at 34.9%, according to ESPN , and they'll be without center Hjalte Froholdt and left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. That's the matchup every one of these picks leans on, with Garrett and Aaron Donald lining up across from a rookie .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The case for the Cardinals is the October game itself. Arizona held the Rams to 16 points with Nacua on the field, and Matthew Stafford has little left to throw to now. A rookie quarterback who protects the ball can keep a game like this one close for a long time.
 We still picked the Rams in this one when we went through the rest of their schedule, and Arizona is 0-3 at home.
